segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics News Digest for October 25, 2026.
Today we cover big updates, including funding for vision-force-action, new humanoid skill training, and a fun new bot arrival.
From The Robot Report, Eka Robotics raises 150 million in Series A funding to scale its vision-force-action model for robots.

This funding supports the expansion of a novel approach where robots develop an intuition of physics through reinforcement learning, allowing them to generalize across objects, tasks, and environments.
The technology enables robots to perform complex actions, such as screwing in a light bulb, by understanding underlying physics instead of relying on human demonstrations.
The company utilizes a simulation learning approach to reduce the simulation to real-world barrier, facilitating the generation of extensive robot experience.
This methodology is seen as a path toward scalable and performant dexterous manipulation capabilities in robotics.
This development indicates a significant step in achieving physically grounded and generalized artificial intelligence for physical systems.
From Humanoid.guide, Unitree develops Rehearsal to improve humanoid robot skills.
This report details a system aimed at enhancing humanoid robot capabilities through an integrated AI workflow involving research analysis, code generation, simulation, and physical testing.
The process involves an AI workflow where research papers are analyzed, code is written, and simulations are run prior to physical trials on the robots.
Unitree already utilizes artificial intelligence to gather feedback from physical tests to refine its models, focusing development on the feedback loop between simulated tests and physical trials.
The company forecasts that robots could complete eighty percent of voice-assigned tasks by twenty twenty eight, encompassing factory and household work.
This development signifies a focus on closing the gap between virtual simulation and real-world robotic performance in the advancement of artificial intelligence systems.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, MagicBot D1!".
This segment details the introduction of the MagicBot D1, an industrial wheeled humanoid designed for factory, warehouse, and research applications.
The robot features an omnidirectional mobile base, a liftable torso, and two highly dexterous arms with seven degrees of freedom and force control for manipulation tasks.

Measuring one hundred eighty centimeters tall and weighing one hundred fifty kilograms, the D1 possesses a listed strength of ten kilograms and operates at a speed of five point four kilometers per hour.

The system is equipped with various sensors, including cameras and LiDAR, and supports multiple communication protocols for industrial use, with a current price of sixty-five thousand United States dollars.
This development signals further progress in deploying advanced robotic systems within industrial and logistics environments.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, A3 Ultra!".

This report details the introduction of the A3 Ultra, a full-size humanoid robot from AGIBOT designed for commercial service environments, demonstrating a physical presence of 174 centimeters and a mass of 60 kilograms.
The robot incorporates a frame constructed from a magnesium alloy and carbon fiber nylon hybrid, enabling it to execute tasks such as sorting goods and folding clothing.
It operates using an embodied AI processor and various cameras for environmental perception, along with autonomous charging capabilities for extended operation.
Manipulation capability is currently rated as developing, while navigation capabilities are rated lower, indicating a prioritization of handling tasks.
The device is listed as in production with a listed price of fifty thousand United States dollars and integrated safety features.
This development signals continued advancement in the application of embodied artificial intelligence within physical robotics.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, CYBORG R01!".
This report details the development and specifications of the CYBORG R01, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for hazardous industrial environments.
The robot measures one hundred eighty centimeters tall and weighs seventy-five kilograms, developed by Cyborg Robotics in China.
It possesses a humanoid frame with sixty-two degrees of freedom and dexterous hands with sixteen degrees of freedom, enabling the handling of a twenty kilogram payload.
The construction utilizes aluminum and magnesium alloys, and the robot operates with motor torques exceeding four hundred newton metres and a battery runtime of two hours.
Demonstrated capabilities include obstacle avoidance, falling recovery, sorting goods, and product assembly, all managed through advanced camera systems and safety controls.
This technology aims to transfer dangerous physical work from humans to robotic systems.
The production unit is priced at seventy thousand US dollars.
Future developments in industrial automation are expected to follow this progression.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, HONOR D1!".
This report details the development and current capabilities of the HONOR D1, a humanoid robot designed primarily for running and navigation.
The robot measures one hundred sixty-nine centimeters tall and weighs forty-five kilograms.
It features twenty-five degrees of freedom and liquid-cooled joint modules.
Current performance includes obstacle avoidance and the ability to run one hundred meters at a maximum speed of twenty-six kilometers per hour.
The robot is presently rated in the early stage for general humanoid skills, concentrating on locomotion rather than manipulation.
As a prototype, this development signifies HONOR's entry into the field of humanoid robotics, with a listed price of one hundred thousand US dollars.
This development indicates further exploration into mobile robotics and advanced locomotion systems is underway within the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, Welcome, Linker Hand O30!
This segment reports on the specifications and performance metrics of the Linker Hand O30 robotic hand.
The hand is a commercially available product manufactured in China, priced at six thousand United States dollars.
The performance evaluation places the Linker Hand O30 at a score of seven out of ten in the Humanoid.Guide Hand Score, indicating a capable but mature performance level in robotic manipulation tasks.
Further analysis breaks down specific capabilities, noting a rating of four out of five for Degrees of Freedom, which suggests strong dexterity, and a rating of three out of five for Strength.
This dual assessment allows for the evaluation of dexterity and strength in specific robotic applications.
The O30 is a produced item relevant for research and integration into various robotic systems.
This development contributes to the ongoing progression of commercially viable robotic end-effectors available for engineering and research applications.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, RH56BFX!".

This segment reports on the introduction of the RH56BFX, a compact robotic hand from Inspire Robotics, which has received a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of four out of ten regarding dexterity and strength.

The RH56BFX measures seventy-five by one hundred and sixty millimeters and weighs zero point five four kilograms, emphasizing its small physical dimensions and mounting considerations for integration.
The design focuses on responsive, everyday manipulation for human and machine interaction, intentionally avoiding heavy industrial applications.
Performance assessment suggests that prospective users should evaluate the hand based on specific task requirements rather than the overall score.
This development indicates ongoing refinement in the capability of compact robotic manipulators for interactive applications.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, 4NE1 Gen 4!".
This report details the introduction of a new humanoid robot, the 4NE1 Gen 4, developed by NEURA Robotics in Germany, which demonstrates advanced capabilities in industrial and domestic assistance.
The robot measures 180 centimeters in height and weighs 65 kilograms, incorporating textile skin, electric actuators, and onboard computing.
It possesses capabilities including sorting goods, product assembly, and domestic tasks such as folding clothes, achieved through 55 degrees of freedom and multi-sensor interaction.
Operation relies on the NEURON AI model, integrating vision, touch, and force sensing for physical interaction.
Availability is currently established in production at a listed price of seventy thousand US dollars.
This development indicates ongoing progress in the practical application of sophisticated AI in physical robotics.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, CYBORG W01!".
This segment details the introduction of the CYBORG W01, a wheeled humanoid robot developed by Cyborg Robotics designed for industrial sorting and assembly tasks.
The robot measures one hundred sixty centimeters in height and weighs one hundred seventy kilograms, featuring articulated arms with five-fingered hands and fifty-three degrees of freedom.
Its construction utilizes an aluminum and magnesium alloy structure, powered by an onboard processor with twelve cores and two hundred seventy-five tera operations per second of compute.
The system incorporates obstacle avoidance and goods sorting capabilities supported by various sensing equipment.
This robot is currently listed in production with a price point of sixty thousand US dollars.
The development of such specialized robotic hardware indicates continued advancement in practical industrial automation and dexterous machine learning applications.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Eka Robotics is really powering up the future.
Thanks for tuning into your daily dose of robot revolution.
Until tomorrow, keep building!
